Executive summary

The business could not agree on its own revenue figure. Three teams produced three numbers from three exports, and meetings were spent reconciling them rather than acting on them. PulseAnalytics exists to make one number, agreed once, available to everyone who needs it — and to make it trustworthy enough that nobody rebuilds it by hand.

Release 1 delivers an automated nightly warehouse, five role-specific dashboards, a real-time trading and payments view, seven analytical models, and a data-quality gate that holds publication when the data is not safe to publish. Every metric is defined once and consumed everywhere from that definition.

Requirements delivered12 of 12 business requirements; 38 of 38 functional requirements. Three are delivered with a stated limitation (BR-07, BR-09, NFR-14).
Verification223 automated tests; 64 data-quality checks; every acceptance criterion mapped to an executable check in section 16.
Principal residual riskMarketing incrementality is a before/after proxy, not an experiment. It informs budget decisions and is labelled as approximate wherever it appears.
RecommendationAccept Release 1. Prioritise a geo-holdout capability and source-side change capture for Release 2.

Business context

Problem statement

The organisation trades through web, mobile, marketplace and physical channels across six regions. Transactional data exists and is accurate at source. The problem is not missing data; it is that no shared, trusted, timely view of it exists.

Observed problems and their business consequence
IDProblemConsequence
P-01Three teams quote three different revenue figuresDecision meetings are spent reconciling numbers instead of deciding. No definition is written down, so each reconciliation starts again.
P-02Reporting is manual and takes 5–10 working daysMonth-end decisions are made on data that is already stale. Nobody asks exploratory questions because each one costs a day.
P-03Payment failures are discovered the next morningA gateway degradation on a Friday evening costs a full night of orders before anyone knows.
P-04Churn is visible only in hindsightRetention effort is spent on customers who have already gone, and the customers who are about to go are not identified.
P-05Marketing return is quoted without a stated attribution basisBudget is allocated on a number nobody can define. Upper-funnel channels are systematically under-funded.
P-06Replenishment is decided on judgementSimultaneous stockouts on fast lines and overstock on slow ones; working capital is trapped where it earns nothing.
P-07No way to tell a data problem from a business problemWhen a number looks wrong, there is no evidence to say whether the business changed or the pipeline broke, so the number is distrusted either way.

Scope

Scope boundaries and the reason for each exclusion
ExcludedReason
Write-back to source systemsThe platform is read-only by design. Write-back makes it part of the transactional critical path and changes its availability requirement entirely.
Individual-level PII reportingAnalysis operates on aggregates and segments. Named-customer lists are limited to the retention call list, which is access-controlled and justified by a specific business process.
Statutory financial reportingThe platform is a management-information system. It reconciles to the ledger; it is not the ledger.
Real-time personalisation to the storefrontRequires sub-second serving and a different availability class. The event stream would support it; nothing else here would.
Predictive stock allocation across locationsRequires per-location demand history the source does not currently provide.

Use case diagram

Use case specifications

Use case summary
IDUse casePrimary actorGoal and success condition
UC-01Review trading performanceExecutiveSee revenue, margin, orders and customer counts for the trailing 90 days against the prior 90. Succeeds when every figure carries a comparison.
UC-02Analyse revenue driversMerchandisingDecompose a revenue change into volume, price and category mix. Succeeds when the three components sum exactly to the total change.
UC-03Evaluate campaign returnMarketingSee return per campaign and per channel on a stated attribution basis, with alternatives. Succeeds when the basis is visible alongside the figure.
UC-04Segment the customer baseMarketingObtain behavioural segments with a recommended action per segment. Succeeds when segments are reproducible from the same dataset.
UC-05Target customers at riskMarketing / CRMObtain a ranked list of currently-active customers likely to lapse. Succeeds when ranked by value at risk and excludes already-churned customers.
UC-06Plan replenishmentMerchandisingObtain a prioritised purchase list with quantities. Succeeds when quantities reflect measured demand variability and a chosen service level.
UC-07Monitor live tradingOperationsSee orders, revenue, payment failures and stock alerts as they happen. Succeeds when the view reflects events within five minutes.
UC-08Forecast demandMerchandisingObtain a revenue and unit forecast with an uncertainty range. Succeeds when the model is selected by backtest against a naive baseline.
UC-09Ingest batch extractOrder systemLand the nightly extract without rejecting rows. Supports UC-01 to UC-06, UC-08.
UC-10Ingest live eventsGateway / storefrontLand order, payment, stock and activity events durably. Supports UC-07.
UC-11Enforce data qualityPlatformVerify the warehouse before publication and hold it when unsafe. Included by UC-09 and UC-10.
UC-12Restate to local currencyFX serviceExpress regional revenue in local currency with the rate and rate date shown. Extends UC-01.
UC-13Operate the pipelineData analystRun, monitor and correct the pipeline; see what ran, how long and what broke.

UC-05 — Target customers at risk (expanded)

Primary actorMarketing / CRM manager
TriggerWeekly retention cycle
PreconditionsThe warehouse has been rebuilt and the quality suite passed. At least one full churn observation window of history exists.
Main flow1. The platform scores every customer whose lifecycle status is not Churned. 2. Each score is multiplied by the customer's projected annual value to give revenue at risk. 3. Customers are banded Low / Medium / High / Critical. 4. The manager works the list from the top. 5. Interventions are recorded outside the platform.
Alternative flowIf the observation window contains only one outcome class, the model cannot be fitted; the platform reports this rather than returning a degenerate score.
PostconditionsA ranked list exists and is exportable. Model quality (holdout AUC) and the drivers of risk are shown alongside it.
Business ruleAlready-churned customers are excluded. They are a win-back problem, not a retention one, and including them floods the list with people it is too late to save.
AcceptanceAC-05 (section 15)

Data requirements

Conceptual model

Agreed metric definitions

These definitions are the commercial contract. Each is implemented once and consumed everywhere from that implementation.

Agreed definitions of the headline metrics
MetricAgreed definitionDecision embedded in it
RevenueNet value of completed orders: gross less discounts, excluding shipping and tax.Shipping and tax are pass-throughs, not earnings. Cancelled and returned orders are retained and flagged, not deleted.
Gross profitRevenue less product cost.Product cost only. No fulfilment or overhead allocation, because the source does not carry it and inventing one would present a fabricated figure as measured.
Average order valueRevenue divided by completed orders, computed at order level.Computed at order level, never averaged from order lines — the latter answers a different question and gives a materially smaller number.
ChurnNo completed order within the churn window (default 90 days) of the analysis date.The window is a business choice and is configurable. A quarterly-cadence business would need a longer one.
Repeat rateCustomers with two or more orders, as a share of customers with at least one.Denominator is purchasers, not all customers — otherwise activation and retention are conflated.
CohortThe calendar month of a customer's first completed order.First purchase, not signup. A signup that never bought is an activation problem wearing a retention costume.
Return on ad spendAttributed revenue divided by spend, on the stated attribution basis.Profit-based return above 1.0 is the meaningful break-even; revenue-based return above 1.0 can still be a loss.
Cost of acquisitionSpend divided by attributed new customers.New customers only. Counting all attributed customers treats existing customers as acquisitions and understates cost.
Payment successTwo measures: failure rate across all attempts (gateway health) and success rate per order on the final attempt (customer experience).A decline recovered on retry is invisible to the customer and very visible to the gateway. One ambiguous rate would be argued about in every review.
Days of coverStock on hand divided by daily sell-through.Undefined, not infinite, where a product sells nothing.
Conversion rateSessions reaching purchase as a share of sessions, on a session basis.Session-based, so a visitor viewing ten products is one session, not ten — which is why the funnel cannot exceed 100%.

Reporting requirements

Required views by audience
ViewAudienceMust answerRefresh
ExecutiveCommercial Director, executive teamIs the business healthy, what changed, and what needs attention this weekDaily
SalesSales and merchandisingWhat sold, why the number moved, which products and regions to act onDaily
CustomersCRM, marketingWho is valuable, who is leaving, which cohorts are improvingDaily
MarketingMarketing managerWhat the spend bought, on what basis, and where to move budgetDaily
OperationsOperations, data platformPayment health, stock actions, funnel losses, pipeline and data qualityDaily
Real timeOperationsWhat is happening right now and what needs interventionContinuous
Insight reportAll, month-endA written narrative with the supporting extractsOn demand
Why the real-time view is not in the BI tool A scheduled import refresh cannot deliver sub-minute latency. Presenting a fifteen-minute-old figure as "live" would be worse than not offering it, so the live view is served by the platform directly and the BI tool covers the curated daily model.

Assumptions, constraints and dependencies

Assumptions
IDAssumptionIf it proves false
AS-01Source systems are accurate at the point of capture; defects are in transfer and integration, not in the transaction itself.Quality thresholds would need to be reset and the repair logic reconsidered.
AS-02A nightly batch cadence is sufficient for commercial decision-making, with real time reserved for operational response.The batch layer would need incremental or streaming ingestion; the stage boundaries already accommodate this.
AS-03The order management system's campaign stamp is the organisation's accepted attribution basis.Attribution would need a dedicated tracking capability upstream.
AS-04Product cost is a sufficient basis for margin at management-reporting level.A cost allocation model would be required, with Finance owning the allocation rules.
AS-05Stakeholders will adopt the agreed definitions rather than maintaining parallel spreadsheets.The platform would deliver technical capability without the business outcome. This is the largest non-technical risk.
Constraints and dependencies
IDTypeDetail
CN-01TeamTwo people build and operate the platform. Operational surface must stay within that capacity.
CN-02DataAttribution is limited to what the source records: one campaign per order, last touch.
CN-03DataNo history of loyalty-tier changes is available at source, which blocks the tier-at-time-of-purchase view.
CN-04CostNon-production infrastructure must be destroyable and rebuildable rather than left running.
DP-01DependencyNightly extract delivered by the order management system.
DP-02DependencyEvent feeds from the payment gateway, storefront and warehouse systems.
DP-03DependencyAn on-call arrangement, required before NFR-14 can be closed.
DP-04DependencyMarketing agreement to withhold spend in a holdout, required for genuine incrementality.

Risks

Business risks
IDRiskImpactLikelihoodMitigation
RSK-01Budget decisions are taken on an incrementality figure that is a proxyHighCertainLabelled as approximate wherever displayed; five attribution models published so the spread is visible. Resolved only by a holdout experiment (DP-04).
RSK-02Stakeholders continue to maintain parallel spreadsheetsHighMediumDefinitions agreed with Finance before build; every figure carries its definition. Ultimately an adoption matter, not a technical one.
RSK-03A pipeline failure goes unnoticed because nothing is routed to a personMediumMediumRun status and quality results visible on the Operations dashboard and via the API. Closing requires DP-03.
RSK-04Source data drifts in a way that is structurally valid but semantically wrongMediumMediumCurrent checks detect broken data, not drifted data. Quality history is retained as the basis for profiling.
RSK-05Churn model degrades as customer behaviour changesMediumMediumModel quality reported with every run; a falling holdout score is visible rather than silent.
RSK-06Key-person dependency in a two-person teamMediumMediumEverything is code, documented and reproducible from one command; no manual step exists in the build.
RSK-07Retention call list contains personal dataMediumLowAccess-controlled, justified by a defined business process, and the only named-customer output in the platform.

Acceptance criteria

Each criterion is verified by an executable check, not by inspection.

Acceptance criteria and their verification
IDBRCriterionResult
AC-01BR-01Revenue computed from order lines equals revenue computed from order headers, and both equal the totals in every aggregate that reports revenue.Pass
AC-02BR-02A full rebuild completes unattended from raw data to published marts, and records every stage.Pass
AC-03BR-03Introducing a genuine defect causes the quality suite to fail; removing it causes the suite to pass.Pass
AC-04BR-03A data failure and a code failure produce different outcomes, so they can be routed differently.Pass
AC-05BR-06Every scored customer receives a probability between 0 and 1; already-churned customers are excluded; the list is ordered by value at risk.Pass
AC-06BR-06The churn model's inputs are demonstrably drawn from before the outcome window, so no future information is used.Pass
AC-07BR-07All attribution models credit the same total revenue, differing only in how it is distributed.Pass
AC-08BR-04Volume, price and mix effects sum exactly to the reported revenue change.Pass
AC-09BR-04The conversion funnel decreases monotonically at every step.Pass
AC-10BR-05Events are not lost when the consuming process is interrupted mid-batch.Pass
AC-11BR-05Replaying a recorded stream reproduces the same live figures it originally produced.Pass
AC-12BR-08Recommended buffer stock increases with demand variability, and a higher service level never reduces it.Pass
AC-13BR-10Two runs from the same inputs produce byte-identical outputs.Pass
AC-14BR-11The selected forecast model is chosen by backtest, and the naive baseline is reported alongside it.Pass
AC-15BR-12Every converted figure displays the rate and rate date used, and substitute rates are identifiable.Pass
AC-16BR-04No chart uses two value axes, and no chart conveys meaning by colour alone.Pass

Glossary and sign-off

Business glossary
TermMeaning
Analysis dateThe latest date present in the data, used as "today" by every recency-based measure so results are reproducible.
AttributionThe rule assigning credit for an order to a marketing activity. This platform ships last touch and publishes alternatives.
Churn windowThe period without a purchase after which a customer is considered lost. Default 90 days; configurable.
CohortCustomers grouped by the month of their first purchase.
IncrementalityRevenue that would not have occurred without the activity. Estimated here by a baseline comparison, not measured by experiment.
Lifetime valueTotal profit expected from a customer relationship. Reported as observed and projected, separately.
RFMSegmentation by recency, frequency and monetary value, scored in quintiles.
Safety stockBuffer inventory covering demand variability during resupply. Driven by variability, not volume.
Service levelThe probability of not running out during resupply. A commercial choice; higher costs more stock.
SessionOne continuous visit. The counting unit for the conversion funnel.
